arxiv-2011-14109.title: A general family of MSRD codes and PMDS codes with smaller field sizes from extended Moore matrices
arxiv-2011-14109.creator: Umberto Martínez-Peñas
arxiv-2011-14109.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Umberto Martínez-Peñas. We construct six new explicit families of linear maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes, each of which has the smallest field sizes among all known MSRD codes for some parameter regime. Using them and a previous result of the author, we provide two new explicit families of linear partial MDS (PMDS) codes with smaller field sizes than previous PMDS codes for some parameter regimes.

arxiv-2103-12172.title: Non-Iterative Domain Decomposition for the Helmholtz Equation Using the Method of Difference Potentials Note: Work supported by the US Army Research Office (ARO) under grant W911NF-16-1-0115 and the US–Israel Binational Science Foundation (BSF) under grant 2014048. Journal: Journal of Computational
arxiv-2103-12172.creator: Evan North, Semyon Tsynkov, Eli Turkel
arxiv-2103-12172.description: Abstract We use the Method of Difference Potentials (MDP) to solve a non-overlapping domain decomposition formulation of the Helmholtz equation. The MDP reduces the Helmholtz equation on each subdomain to a Calderon’s boundary equation with projection on its boundary. The unknowns for the Calderon’s equation are the Dirichlet and Neumann data.

arxiv-2302-01773.title: Absence of fractal quantum criticality in the quantum Newman-Moore model
arxiv-2302-01773.creator: Raymond Wiedmann, Lea Lenke, Matthias Mühlhauser, Kai Phillip Schmidt
arxiv-2302-01773.description: Abstract The quantum phase transition between the low-field fracton phase with type-II fracton excitations and the high-field polarized phase is investigated in the two-dimensional self-dual quantum Newman-Moore model. We apply perturbative and numerical linked-cluster expansions to calculate the ground-state energy per site in the thermodynamic limit revealing a level crossing at the self-dual point.

arxiv-2302-04789.title: Learning in Quantum Common-Interest Games and the Separability Problem
arxiv-2302-04789.creator: Wayne Lin, Georgios Piliouras, Ryann Sim, Antonios Varvitsiotis
arxiv-2302-04789.description: Abstract Learning in games has emerged as a powerful tool for machine learning with numerous applications. Quantum games model interactions between strategic players who have access to quantum resources, and several recent works have studied learning in the competitive regime of quantum zero-sum games.

arxiv-2509-01545.title: Complex spectral variability and hints of a luminous companion in the Be star + black hole binary candidate ALS 8814
arxiv-2509-01545.creator: Kareem El-Badry 1,2, Matthias Fabry 3, Hugues Sana 4,5, Tomer Shenar 6, Rhys Seeburger 2
arxiv-2509-01545.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kareem El-Badry 1,2, Matthias Fabry 3, Hugues Sana 4,5, Tomer Shenar 6, Rhys Seeburger 2. The emission-line binary ALS 8814 was recently proposed as a Be star + black hole (BH) binary based on large-amplitude radial velocity (RV) variations of a Be star and non-detection of spectroscopic features from a luminous companion. We reanalyze low- and medium-resolution LAMOST spectra of ALS 8814 and show that the system’s spectroscopic variability is considerably more complex than previously recognized.

pmc-11479367.title: A Piezoresistive-Sensor Nonlinearity Correction on-Chip Method with Highly Robust Class-AB Driving Capability
pmc-11479367.creator: Kai Jing, Yuhang Han, Shaoxiong Yuan, Rong Zhao, Jiabo Cao
pmc-11479367.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This paper presents a thorough robust Class-AB power amplifier design and its application in pressure-mode sensor-on-chip nonlinearity correction. Considering its use in piezoresistive sensing applications, a gain-boosting-aided folded cascode structure is utilized to increase the amplifier’s gain by a large amount as well as enhancing the power rejection ability, and a push–pull structure with miller compensation, a floating gate technique, and an adaptive output driving limiting structures are adopted to achieve high-efficiency current driving capability, high stability, and electronic environmental compatibility.
